Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Aftab Alam, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Anit Kumar Shukla, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. This is the second bail application on behalf of the applicant.
The first one was rejected by this Court vide order dated 30.01.2023.
4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 66 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sector- Bara, District Prayagraj, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the marriage of applicant was solemnized with the sister of the informant as per Hindu rites about one year before her death.
The applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected her to cruelty for demand of dowry leading her to death on 28.03.2019 at 02:00 A.M.

The FIR was instituted on the same night at 11:00 P.M.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that there are general and omnibus allegations against all the accused persons.
The door of the room was broken open which clearly indicates that this is suicidal case as no injury was observed by the doctor, who conducted the autopsy of the deceased and viscera was preserved.
The viscera report indicates that carbofuran insecticide was consumed by the deceased.
It was the applicant who had admitted the deceased to the hospital.
Learned counsel further stated that six witnesses of fact have been examined so far and charge-sheet indicates that there are a large number of witnesses who are yet to be examined.
There is no likelihood of conclusion of trial in near future as the trial is moving at a snails pace.
Learned counsel has stated that fundamental rights of the applicant enshrined under article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 18.04.2019.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance upon the judgment of Supreme Court in case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.
7.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. The Apex Court in the case of Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712, has observed as under:-
"We are conscious of the fact that the charges levelled against the respondent are grave and a serious threat to societal harmony.

entities.text: Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Had it been a case at the threshold,
we would have outrightly turned down the respondent's prayer.

However, keeping in mind the length of the period spent by him in custody and the unlikelihood of the trial being completed anytime soon, the High Court appears to have been left with no other option except to grant bail."

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, period of custody and the fact that the trial is moving at snails pace and also taking into consideration the judgments of Supreme Court, passed in the case of K.A. Najeeb (supra) and Satender Kumar Antil (supra), and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant- Deshraj Bind involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
11.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
12.
It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witness.
